Annual profit targets can sit beside sales and share objectives.

So the statement is True.

Marketing that attracts profitable customer segments supports profitability objectives directly. Not every buyer is equally worth winning; segment choice is part of how profit aims get met.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit is internal finance for marketing initiatives.

So the statement is True.

Sales and profit usually move together, but exceptions exist. Discount wars, cost spikes, and bad mix can break the positive link, which is why the chapter refuses a blind “more sales, always more profit” rule.

Dissatisfied customers rarely buy again, so satisfaction failures also threaten future sales and, downstream, profit. The interdependence runs through repurchase: unhappy buyers exit, volume suffers, and profitability objectives get harder to hit.

So the statement is True.

Profitability objectives remind managers that revenue growth must outpace cost growth — otherwise the “growth” is hollow.

So the statement is True.

title: Comprehensive Objective Assertions
context: Analyze how a unique selling proposition makes a product seem special, unique, or better than alternatives. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Retained profit cannot support production capacity expansion.
A profitability objective is fulfilled when the firm has the most employees.
A business may analyse contribution margin per unit to support profit objectives.
Marketing that raises sales with rising costs always increases profit.
Profitability is excluded when businesses analyse customer wishes and needs.
tactical_explanations:
Retained profit can fund production capacity expansion — that is a standard use of plough-back.

So the statement is False.

Having the most employees does not fulfil a profitability objective. Headcount is not surplus.

So the statement is False.

Contribution margin per unit is a practical lens for profit objectives: it shows what each sale leaves after variable cost toward covering fixed costs and profit.

So the statement is True.

Sales up with costs rising faster need not raise profit — the cost chase can erase the volume gain. “Always increases profit” is the false absolute.

A USP that makes the product feel special can lift willingness to pay, which helps the profit side when costs behave. But marketing that only inflates volume while costs race ahead fails the profitability test. Uniqueness in buyers’ minds is not a free pass past cost arithmetic.

So the statement is False.

Analysing customer wishes and needs does not exclude profitability. Market analysis informs objectives that still include profit among the set.

So the statement is False.

title: Late-Stage USP and Share Cases
context: Review the marketing objective of maintaining sales volume to generate revenue. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profits reimburse owners and can be ploughed back into the business per the text.
Marketing objectives on profit recognise limitations when discounting erodes margins.
Higher sales volume increases the revenue pool from which profit is calculated after costs.
Profit retention funds improvements that may later support customer satisfaction.
Profits are important only for tax purposes and not for reinvestment.
tactical_explanations:
Profits reimburse owners and can be ploughed back into the firm.

So the statement is True.

Profit objectives build in the risk that discounting erodes margins even when volume rises — that limitation shapes how serious profit targets are written.

So the statement is True.

Higher sales volume enlarges the revenue pool from which profit is calculated after costs. More pool does not guarantee more profit, but it is the starting feedstock.

So the statement is True.

Retaining profit can fund improvements that later support customer satisfaction — better service systems, quality fixes, training — paid from earnings kept inside.

Maintaining sales volume to generate revenue is the ongoing commercial heartbeat; profit retention is how that heartbeat also finances future satisfaction and competitiveness. Treating profits as tax-only trivia ignores that reinvestment role entirely.

So the statement is True.

Profits matter for reinvestment and owner return, not only for tax forms.

So the statement is False.

title: Terminal Profit and Sales Review
context: Analyze how retained profit from higher sales can be reinvested in the business. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability assessment includes whether marketing achieved cost-effective sales growth.
Owners' invested money is reimbursed through profits earned from successful operations.
A firm may delay profit growth while investing heavily in brand and USP development.
Profit reinvestment is a strategic use of earnings kept within the business.
Limitations on sales-driven profit include simultaneous increases in marketing expenditure.
tactical_explanations:
Profitability checks whether marketing delivered cost-effective sales growth.

So the statement is True.

Owners’ invested money is reimbursed through profits earned from successful operations. That capital-return path is central to why profitability earns a place among marketing-linked business aims.

So the statement is True.

Firms may accept delayed profit growth while they invest heavily in brand and USP development. Short-term surplus is traded for longer-term positioning — a conscious sequence, not accidental neglect.

So the statement is True.

Profit reinvestment is the strategic use of earnings kept in the business: capacity, marketing assets, or product work funded internally.

Higher sales can create the retained profit that gets reinvested, but limitations apply when marketing expenditure rises in step with volume. The sales-driven profit story stays conditional on those cost and spend patterns, which is why assessment looks at cost-effectiveness, not volume alone.

So the statement is True.

Sales-driven profit weakens when marketing spend rises in step with volume.

So the statement is True.

title: Marketing Case 100
context: Review the interdependence of customer satisfaction, differentiation, market share, sales, and profitability objectives. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Profitability and sales objectives are interrelated but not identical measures.
Marketing performance should ultimately contribute to sustainable profitability.
Retained profit strengthens the balance sheet for future marketing campaigns.
Profit per unit may fall even when total sales volume rises if prices are cut sharply.
Marketing objectives exclude profitability whenever sales volume targets are set.
tactical_explanations:
Profitability and sales are related measures, not identical ones.

So the statement is True.

Marketing performance should ultimately contribute to sustainable profitability. Soft wins on awareness or volume that never clear costs fail the commercial end-test the objective set is aiming at.

So the statement is True.

Retained profit strengthens the balance sheet for future marketing campaigns, giving the firm internal equity cushion to fund the next push without relying only on new borrowing.

So the statement is True.

Sharp price cuts can lift total volume while cutting profit per unit. The firm sells more and earns less on each ticket — a clean illustration that sales and profitability objectives can diverge.

Satisfaction, differentiation, share, sales, and profitability interdepend, but they are not fused into one number. A plan that sets volume targets still keeps profitability in the objective set; excluding profit whenever sales targets appear would break that interdependence the stem asks you to review.

So the statement is True.

Sales volume targets do not exclude profitability from the marketing objective set.

So the statement is False.

title: Product Orientation Versus Market Orientation
context: Review how product-oriented and market-oriented businesses differ in where they place initial emphasis when developing offerings. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A product-oriented business first analyses customers' needs and wants before defining product specifications.
A product-oriented business focuses on the product and its specifications first and later thinks about how to sell it.
A market-oriented business will first analyse customers' needs and wants and then tailor products to fulfil these requirements.
Product-oriented and market-oriented businesses may pursue identical marketing objectives even when their strategic starting points differ.
A product-oriented business mainly relies on the quality of the features of the product to be successful in the market.
tactical_explanations:
Product orientation does not begin with a customer-needs survey. It begins inside the firm: engineers and product managers lock the features, materials, and specs they intend to build, and only afterwards ask how those finished goods will be sold.

The claim reverses that order. Saying the product-oriented firm “first analyses customers’ needs and wants before defining specifications” describes market orientation — the path that maps demand, then designs to match. A workshop that finalises a modular sofa range in the design studio before any shopper interviews is product-oriented, not needs-first.

So the statement is False.

A product-oriented business locks the product and its specifications.

So the statement is True.

Market orientation flips the sequence: the firm studies what customers need and want, then shapes the offering to meet those requirements. A fashion buyer who surveys seasonal style shifts before commissioning new lines is working market-first — needs analysis leads, specification follows, and promotion is built around the demand signal rather than around an already frozen SKU list.

So the statement is True.

Orientation is about starting point, not about the scoreboard. Two rivals can chase the same market-share or satisfaction target while one freezes specs in the lab (product-led) and the other redesigns after every survey wave (market-led). Identical objectives do not require identical strategic starting points.

So the statement is True.

Product-oriented success stories lean on feature quality — durability, polish, technical edge — as the main reason buyers should choose the item. Selling plans come later; the bet is that strong features carry the market case.

So the statement is True.

title: Focus on Features or Customer Needs
context: Analyze the contrast between focusing on product features and focusing on customers' needs and wants in marketing orientation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: The market-oriented approach has the advantage of anticipating changing needs and wants and responding to market changes earlier than product-oriented competitors.
Market-oriented businesses define specifications first and only later consider whether buyers want those features.
Product-oriented and market-oriented businesses must always pursue completely different marketing objectives.
A product-oriented business ignores product quality and relies solely on aggressive advertising without strong features.
Market-oriented businesses cannot anticipate changing needs because they focus only on current specifications.
tactical_explanations:
Market orientation’s timing edge is real: by watching shifting wants continuously, the firm can redesign or reprice before a product-led rival finishes its next internal specification cycle. A grocery chain that sees plant-based demand rising and restocks within weeks beats a competitor still locked to last year’s assortment plan.

That earlier response is the advantage the chapter associates with market orientation over specification-first rivals.

So the statement is True.

Market-oriented firms do the opposite of “specs first, buyers later”.

So the statement is False.

Shared marketing objectives are allowed across orientations. A product-led and a market-led firm can both pursue higher satisfaction or share; what differs is whether they start from the catalogue or from the customer. Claiming they must always chase completely different objectives confuses starting method with goal labels.

So the statement is False.

Product orientation does not abandon quality for empty advertising. The classic product-led bet is that strong features sell; aggressive ads without a solid offering would undercut that logic. A furniture maker that pours craft into joinery and materials is product-oriented precisely because it trusts feature quality, not because it ignores features.

A supermarket cardholder trading a name and email for weekly dairy discounts accepts less anonymity because the benefit feels worth it.

So the statement is False.

Market orientation exists to anticipate change. Saying such firms “cannot anticipate” because they only watch current specs mislabels them as product-oriented. Tracking evolving needs is the core market-led practice, not a barrier to it.

So the statement is False.

title: Identical Objectives With Different Orientations
context: Review why many businesses have moved from product orientation towards a market-oriented approach over recent decades. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Which orientation is more suitable for a business largely depends on the product itself and the number of competitors in the market.
Orientation suitability is identical for every product regardless of competitive conditions or product characteristics.
Markets and the expectations of customers should not be neglected even when a firm emphasises internal product development.
Customer relationship management aims at creating a long-term relationship with customers rather than treating each sale as isolated.
CRM systems keep customer data so the business can mail or email newsletters, coupons, and product information to encourage repeat purchases.
tactical_explanations:
Which orientation fits better depends on the product itself and on how many competitors crowd the market. Sparse rivalry and highly technical goods can still reward a feature-first craft path; dense rivalry with fast-changing tastes usually rewards market-led listening.

So the statement is True.

Orientation suitability is not identical for every product regardless of rivals or product traits.

So the statement is False.

Even a firm that invests heavily in internal product development still cannot treat markets as optional. Customer expectations keep moving; rivals who listen will pull share if the lab-focused firm never checks whether buyers still want those polished features. Strong internal R&D and market attention are not mutually exclusive — neglecting the market side is the risk the chapter flags.

So the statement is True.

CRM is built for long-term relationships, not isolated one-off sales: retained profiles support return visits, not a single checkout and goodbye.

So the statement is True.

CRM systems keep customer data so the firm can mail or email newsletters, coupons, and product updates that nudge repeat purchases. A garage that stores motorists’ service dates and later sends a seasonal maintenance coupon is using retained records exactly that way — contact between purchases, not a wiped slate after each visit.

Without those stored addresses and histories, the “encourage them to come back” channel disappears.

So the statement is True.

title: Market-Oriented Anticipation of Change
context: Consider a fashion retailer that surveys changing style preferences each season before commissioning new garment lines from suppliers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sensitive use of personal customer data is indispensable when businesses build detailed CRM profiles.
By using personal accounts and loyalty cards, customers often give up their anonymity willingly in order to receive discounts and special offers.
Strong product specifications allow a business to ignore markets and customer expectations entirely.
Many businesses collect data on their customers and their buying behaviours so they can tailor offers to personal preferences.
Product orientation emphasises focus on production and product features rather than on customers' needs and wants at the initial stage.
tactical_explanations:
Detailed CRM profiles are built from personal data, so sensitive handling is indispensable — not a nice-to-have footnote.

So the statement is True.

Loyalty cards and personal accounts routinely trade anonymity for discounts and special offers. Shoppers who enrol know the retailer can link purchases to an identity; they accept that visibility because the price benefits feel worth it. The chapter treats that willing exchange as normal CRM practice, not as an accidental leak.

Two rivals can chase the same margin while one locks a fixed catalogue in HQ and the other reshapes offers after every survey wave.

So the statement is True.

Strong specifications never license a firm to ignore markets and customer expectations entirely.

So the statement is False.

Many businesses collect data on customers and buying behaviour precisely so offers can be tailored to personal preferences — preferred sizes, diet tags, past categories — rather than blasting one generic flyer to everyone.

So the statement is True.

Product orientation places initial emphasis on production and product features, not on customers’ needs and wants. A cosmetics lab that freezes formulation and packaging before studying beauty-trend shifts is acting product-first: the catalogue leads, and selling logic follows after the features are locked.

That is the opposite of a season-by-season preference survey that commissions garments only after tastes are mapped.

So the statement is True.

title: Product Quality as Primary Market Strategy
context: Review the market-oriented advantage of anticipating changing customer needs and responding earlier than product-oriented rivals. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Customer relationship management aims only at single-transaction sales without building long-term customer relationships.
Market orientation emphasises focus on customers' needs and wants when deciding what to produce and promote.
CRM systems delete customer data immediately after each purchase so no newsletters or coupons can be sent later.
Sensitive use of personal data is optional and unnecessary when businesses operate loyalty programmes.
Loyalty cards and personal accounts always preserve full customer anonymity without any identifiable records.
tactical_explanations:
CRM is not a single-transaction machine. Its stated aim is a long-term relationship: remember the customer, stay in contact, and invite the next purchase. Treating CRM as “sell once and forget” erases the retention logic that newsletters, coupons, and account histories are built to support.

A bookstore that emails readers about new titles in categories they already buy is practising relationship CRM, not a one-shot till receipt.

So the statement is False.

Market orientation puts customers’ needs and wants at the centre of what to produce and promote.

So the statement is True.

CRM systems retain customer data after purchase so newsletters and coupons can be sent later — they do not wipe records immediately. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is False.

Sensitive use of personal data is not optional fluff for loyalty programmes. Profiles, cards, and account histories identify people; mishandling that information damages trust and undermines the long-term relationship CRM is meant to build. Calling sensitivity “unnecessary” contradicts how modern loyalty marketing actually works.

A bookstore emailing readers about new titles in categories they already buy is practising relationship CRM, not a one-shot till receipt.

So the statement is False.

Loyalty cards and personal accounts create identifiable records by design; they do not preserve full anonymity.

So the statement is False.

title: Neglecting Customer Expectations
context: Analyze how product-oriented and market-oriented firms may pursue identical marketing objectives yet follow different strategic paths. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Businesses cannot tailor offers to personal preferences because collecting buying-behaviour data is prohibited in CRM.
Product orientation and market orientation differ only in advertising slogans rather than in development focus.
Market orientation means producing whatever engineers prefer without reference to customer requirements.
Over recent decades many businesses have moved from a product-oriented approach towards a market-oriented approach.
CRM discourages repeat purchases by avoiding contact between one sale and the next.
tactical_explanations:
CRM practice actively collects buying-behaviour data so offers can be tailored — it is not prohibited, and personalisation is a core use case.

So the statement is False.

Product and market orientation differ in development focus, not merely in advertising slogans. One starts from specs and features; the other starts from needs and wants. A slogan swap without changing whether the firm designs before or after listening would leave the orientation unchanged.

The chapter’s contrast is about sequence and emphasis in building the offer, not about tagline wording.

So the statement is False.

Market orientation does not mean “produce whatever engineers prefer.

So the statement is False.

Over recent decades many businesses have shifted from product-oriented starting points toward market-oriented ones as competition and changing tastes made listening harder to skip.

So the statement is True.

CRM encourages repeat purchases through contact between sales — newsletters, coupons, reminders — rather than avoiding contact. A fitness studio that emails members after attendance drops is using CRM to reconnect, not to stay silent until the next random walk-in.

Avoiding contact would undercut the long-term relationship goal, not define it. An electronics brand emailing accessory suggestions from a prior laptop purchase is drawing on recorded behaviour, not a blank anonymous visit.

So the statement is False.

title: CRM Long-Term Relationship Goals
context: Review Figure 10 comparing product orientation with market orientation on focus, selling logic, and customer emphasis. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A product-oriented business may believe that a good product sells itself through its features and quality.
Market orientation aligns with producing what customers need and want rather than what internal teams prefer in isolation.
CRM encourages customers to return and buy again through informed contact supported by stored personal records.
Personal data sensitivity has become a very important topic as businesses expand loyalty-driven marketing programmes.
Tailored offers reflect stored knowledge of individual customer preferences derived from purchase histories and account data.
tactical_explanations:
A product-oriented firm may believe strong features make the good sell itself.

So the statement is True.

Market orientation aligns production with what customers need and want, not with what internal teams prefer in isolation. A software team that ships only what engineers find elegant, without checking upgrade demand, is drifting from market orientation; a team that shapes releases around recorded user jobs-to-be-done is closer to the chapter’s market-led principle.

So the statement is True.

CRM encourages return visits through informed contact backed by stored personal records — preferences, dates, past baskets — so the next message is relevant rather than generic.

So the statement is True.

As loyalty-driven marketing expands, personal data sensitivity has become a central topic: more cards, accounts, and profiles mean more identifiable information to protect. Firms that treat sensitivity casually risk trust failures that undo the relationship CRM is meant to deepen.

The chapter links that sensitivity concern directly to the growth of loyalty programmes, not to a side regulatory footnote.

So the statement is True.

Tailored offers work because the firm stores knowledge of individual preferences drawn from purchase histories and account data.

So the statement is True.

title: Sensitive Use of Personal Data
context: Consider a furniture workshop that invests in craftsmanship and material quality before researching whether buyers want modular or traditional designs. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Personal data sensitivity became irrelevant once loyalty programmes began offering discounts.
A market-oriented firm analyses requirements before tailoring products, whereas a product-oriented firm defines specifications before selling.
A market-oriented business believes a good product sells itself without studying customer needs.
Product-oriented firms tailor products to fulfil requirements identified through upfront needs analysis.
Businesses have universally abandoned market orientation and returned entirely to product orientation.
tactical_explanations:
Personal data sensitivity did not become irrelevant when loyalty programmes started offering discounts — if anything, discounts increased how much identifiable data firms hold, so careful handling matters more.

A cosmetics lab that freezes formulation before studying beauty-trend shifts is acting product-first: the catalogue leads, selling logic follows. A garage that emails motorists a seasonal maintenance coupon from stored service dates shows how retained records make the next visit possible.

So the statement is False.

A market-oriented firm analyses requirements before tailoring products; a product-oriented firm defines specifications before selling. That sequence contrast is the chapter’s core orientation distinction.

So the statement is True.

Believing a good product sells itself without studying needs is product-orientation logic, not market orientation. Market-led firms refuse to skip the needs analysis; they do not assume features alone close the sale.

A furniture workshop that never asks whether buyers want modular versus traditional designs, yet trusts craftsmanship to “sell itself,” is product-led in spirit — the opposite of market orientation.

So the statement is False.

Product-oriented firms do not tailor products from upfront needs analysis.

So the statement is False.

Businesses have not universally abandoned market orientation for a full return to product orientation; the long-run shift has been toward market focus.

So the statement is False.

title: Loyalty Cards and Voluntary Anonymity
context: Review the warning that markets and customer expectations should not be neglected even when product quality is strong. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Identical profitability or market-share objectives can coexist with different orientation choices across competing firms.
CRM newsletters and coupons are unrelated to stored customer data and require no personal records.
Product-oriented competitors may respond to market changes later than market-oriented rivals who anticipated shifting wants.
CRM newsletters and coupons sent by email use retained customer data to maintain contact between purchase occasions.
Loyalty cards link identifiable customers to discounts, illustrating willing exchange of anonymity for tangible benefits.
tactical_explanations:
Identical profitability or market-share goals can sit beside different.

So the statement is True.

CRM newsletters and coupons depend on stored customer data; they are not free-floating messages that need no personal records. Without an email, address, or account link, the firm cannot send the coupon to the right person. Claiming those tactics are “unrelated” to retained data reverses how CRM contact actually works.

A supermarket that emails a dairy coupon to a household that buys milk weekly is using a retained behavioural record, not broadcasting into a void.

So the statement is False.

Product-oriented competitors often respond later to market changes than market-oriented rivals who already anticipated shifting wants.

So the statement is True.

Email newsletters and coupons use retained customer data to keep contact alive between purchase occasions — the bridge CRM builds from one visit to the next. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is True.

Loyalty cards link identifiable customers to discounts, showing a willing trade of anonymity for tangible benefits. Enrolment creates a named profile; the shopper accepts that link because the savings or special offers feel worthwhile.

That exchange is exactly the privacy-for-benefits pattern the chapter describes for modern loyalty schemes. A workshop that freezes a sofa range in the design studio before any shopper interviews is living that product-led sequence in miniature.

So the statement is True.

title: Tailoring Offers to Customer Preferences
context: Analyze customer relationship management as a practice aimed at creating long-term relationships with customers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Customers never willingly surrender anonymity because loyalty discounts are always worthless.
Buying-behaviour data is collected only for tax reporting and not for marketing tailoring.
Market-oriented competitors respond later to change because they wait for engineers to finish specifications.
Buying-behaviour records help businesses match promotional content to what individual customers are likely to value.
Product orientation places customers' needs and wants ahead of production and product features at the initial stage.
tactical_explanations:
Customers often do willingly surrender anonymity when loyalty discounts are valuable — the claim that they never do, because discounts are “always worthless,” contradicts everyday card and account enrolment.

A fashion buyer who surveys seasonal style shifts before commissioning new lines is letting needs analysis lead and specification follow. A hotel that installs sleek in-room devices yet never checks whether guests actually use them has quality on paper and market neglect in practice.

So the statement is False.

Buying-behaviour data is collected for marketing tailoring, not merely for tax reporting.

So the statement is False.

Market-oriented competitors are the ones positioned to respond earlier, not later. They watch changing wants and adjust; they do not sit idle until engineers finish an unrelated specification cycle. Saying market-led firms respond later because they “wait for engineers” swaps their label with product orientation.

A bookshop that restocks from category sales data before the quarter starts is accelerating with the market, not lagging behind a lab schedule.

So the statement is False.

Buying-behaviour records help match promotional content to what each customer is likely to value.

So the statement is True.

Product orientation does not place customers’ needs ahead of production and features at the outset — that needs-first order is market orientation. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is False.

title: Product-First Specification Development
context: Review how CRM systems retain customer data to mail or email newsletters, coupons, and product information. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Neglecting evolving customer expectations undermines success even when product specifications remain technically strong.
Orientation choice is fixed by law so every firm in a sector must use market orientation.
Market-oriented businesses tailor products after analysing needs, placing customer focus ahead of final specification choices.
Product-oriented businesses think about selling only after the product and its specifications have been defined internally.
Sensitive handling of personal data supports sustainable CRM rather than eroding trust built through long-term relationships.
tactical_explanations:
Even technically strong specifications fail commercially if evolving.

So the statement is True.

Orientation choice is not fixed by law. Firms in the same sector can choose product-led or market-led starting points depending on product type, rivalry, and strategy. There is no statute that forces every player into market orientation.

Two consumer-electronics brands can sit side by side — one freezing a feature roadmap in R&D, the other reshaping SKUs after every retail panel — and both remain legally free to keep that difference.

So the statement is False.

Market-oriented businesses analyse needs first, then tailor products, keeping customer focus ahead of final specification choices.

So the statement is True.

Product-oriented businesses define the product and its specifications internally first, and only afterwards think in detail about selling. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is True.

Sensitive handling of personal data supports sustainable CRM: trust grows when profiles are protected, and long-term relationships erode when data is treated casually. Retention of emails and histories only works if customers believe the firm will not misuse what they shared for loyalty benefits.

Sensitivity is therefore part of the relationship machinery, not an obstacle to it.

So the statement is True.

title: Needs Analysis Before Product Design
context: Consider a bookshop that analyses reading-category sales data before deciding which new titles to stock for the coming quarter. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: CRM aims at long-term relationships supported by mailing or emailing product information that encourages customers to return.
Customers who register personal accounts often accept reduced anonymity because loyalty schemes deliver discounts and special offers.
Businesses tailor offers to personal preferences after collecting data on customers and their buying behaviours.
CRM long-term relationships require no communication because customers automatically return without contact.
Suitability of product versus market orientation is contingent on product type and competitive conditions rather than fixed by rule.
tactical_explanations:
CRM aims at long-term relationships supported by mailing or emailing product information that encourages customers to return. A bookshop that analyses category sales and then emails readers about new titles in those categories is using retained contact to invite the next visit, not closing the file after one sale.

That ongoing communication is what separates CRM from a one-off till transaction.

So the statement is True.

Customers who register personal accounts often accept less anonymity because loyalty schemes deliver discounts and special offers.

So the statement is True.

After collecting data on customers and buying behaviour, businesses tailor offers to personal preferences — matching content to what each shopper has actually shown they like.

A supermarket cardholder trading a name and email for weekly dairy discounts accepts less anonymity because the benefit feels worth it. A bookstore emailing readers about new titles in categories they already buy is practising relationship CRM, not a one-shot till receipt.

So the statement is True.

CRM long-term relationships need communication; customers do not.

So the statement is False.

Whether product or market orientation fits better depends on product type and competitive conditions, not on a fixed universal rule. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is True.

title: Competitive Timing in Market Orientation
context: Review how personal accounts and loyalty cards lead customers to give up anonymity willingly for discounts and special offers. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sensitive personal data handling matters only for government agencies and not for commercial CRM programmes.
Product orientation centres production and feature development before external customer needs receive detailed attention.
Identical marketing objectives prove that two firms must also share the same orientation starting point.
Market-oriented firms never collect customer data because data collection contradicts customer focus.
Product-oriented businesses never advertise because they assume buyers discover features without promotion.
tactical_explanations:
Sensitive personal-data handling matters for commercial CRM programmes.

So the statement is False.

Product orientation centres production and feature development before external customer needs get detailed attention. Specs and craft lead; the selling story is written once the offering already exists.

So the statement is True.

Identical marketing objectives do not prove two firms share the same orientation starting point. Both can chase satisfaction or share while one is product-led and the other market-led. Objectives describe the scoreboard; orientation describes whether the firm begins with the catalogue or with the customer.

A hotel group and a rival can both target the same occupancy rate yet one freezes a standard points ladder and the other rebuilds offers after every guest survey.

So the statement is False.

Market-oriented firms often collect customer data precisely because customer focus requires evidence of preferences — data collection supports, rather than contradicts, that focus.

So the statement is False.

Product-oriented businesses may still advertise; they do not assume buyers will discover features with zero promotion. The product-led bet is that strong features carry the case, not that marketing spend must be zero.

A hotel that installs sleek in-room devices yet never checks whether guests actually use them has quality on paper and market neglect in practice.

So the statement is False.

title: Orientation Suitability and Product Type
context: Analyze how businesses collect data on customers and buying behaviours to tailor offers to personal preferences. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market orientation places customers' needs and wants at the forefront when shaping what the business will offer.
CRM retention tactics include coupons designed to bring registered customers back for additional purchases.
Personal data sensitivity matters because CRM systems retain identifiable information for ongoing marketing contact.
Loyalty programmes force anonymity on customers who cannot access discounts without remaining unidentified.
Market-oriented firms gain an edge by responding earlier when customer needs and wants begin to change.
tactical_explanations:
Market orientation places customers’ needs and wants at the forefront.

So the statement is True.

CRM retention tactics include coupons meant to bring registered customers back for further purchases — a concrete bridge between one basket and the next. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is True.

Personal data sensitivity matters because CRM systems retain identifiable information for ongoing marketing contact. Names, emails, and card IDs are not anonymous aggregates; mishandling them threatens the trust that keeps people enrolled.

Sensitivity is therefore tied to how CRM actually stores and reuses identity, not to an abstract ethics poster. A hotel that installs sleek in-room devices yet never checks whether guests actually use them has quality on paper and market neglect in practice.

So the statement is True.

Loyalty programmes do not force anonymity; they typically require identification so discounts can be linked to a person.

So the statement is False.

Market-oriented firms gain an edge by responding earlier when needs and wants begin to change — adjusting range or promotion while specification-led rivals are still finishing an internal cycle.

Two rivals can chase the same margin while one locks a fixed catalogue in HQ and the other reshapes offers after every survey wave. A software team shaping releases around recorded user jobs-to-be-done is closer to market orientation than one shipping only what engineers find elegant.

So the statement is True.

title: CRM Newsletters and Repeat Purchases
context: Review the product-oriented view that a good product sells itself through its features rather than through market adaptation. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Product-oriented firms mainly bet on feature quality rather than on continuous market adaptation for success.
Registered loyalty programmes illustrate how customers willingly surrender anonymity to obtain price benefits.
Tailored offers ignore personal preferences because CRM stores only aggregate industry statistics.
Neglecting customer expectations is recommended when product specifications are technically advanced.
CRM is identical to a single promotional campaign with no aim of sustaining relationships over time.
tactical_explanations:
Product-oriented firms mainly bet on feature quality rather than on continuous market adaptation for commercial success.

So the statement is True.

Registered loyalty programmes show customers willingly surrendering anonymity to obtain price benefits — the privacy-for-discount exchange in everyday retail.

A bookstore emailing readers about new titles in categories they already buy is practising relationship CRM, not a one-shot till receipt. A cosmetics lab that freezes formulation before studying beauty-trend shifts is acting product-first: the catalogue leads, selling logic follows.

So the statement is True.

Tailored offers are built from personal preference data, not from aggregate industry statistics alone. CRM stores individual histories so a message can reflect what that shopper bought, not only what the whole sector averages.

If the database held only industry-wide totals, “personalised” coupons would collapse into the same blast for everyone — which is not how chapter CRM tailoring is described.

So the statement is False.

Neglecting customer expectations is not recommended even when specifications.

So the statement is False.

CRM is not identical to a single promotional campaign; it aims to sustain relationships over time through repeated, informed contact. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is False.

title: Buying Behaviour Data Collection
context: Consider a consumer electronics manufacturer that engineers advanced specifications first and only later designs promotional campaigns around those technical features. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Stored customer histories enable businesses to email tailored product information aligned with prior interests.
Personal accounts and loyalty cards never record buying behaviour usable for later marketing contact.
Market orientation eliminates the need to consider product quality because only customer opinions matter.
Product orientation means ignoring production entirely and focusing only on customer service scripts.
Both orientations may target customer satisfaction, yet product orientation still prioritises specifications before selling.
tactical_explanations:
Stored customer histories let businesses email tailored product.

So the statement is True.

Personal accounts and loyalty cards routinely record buying behaviour for later marketing contact — claiming they never do contradicts how those tools are used.

An electronics brand that emails accessory suggestions based on a previous laptop purchase is drawing on recorded behaviour, not on a blank anonymous visit. A bookstore emailing readers about new titles in categories they already buy is practising relationship CRM, not a one-shot till receipt.

So the statement is False.

Market orientation does not eliminate product quality. Customer opinions guide what to make, but the resulting goods still need to perform; “only opinions matter, quality irrelevant” is a caricature, not the chapter’s market-led principle.

An electronics brand emailing accessory suggestions from a prior laptop purchase is drawing on recorded behaviour, not a blank anonymous visit.

So the statement is False.

Product orientation does not mean ignoring production to focus only on service scripts; it emphasises production and features first.

So the statement is False.

Both orientations may aim at customer satisfaction, yet product orientation still prioritises specifications before the selling plan. Satisfaction is a shared destination; sequence is what differs.

So the statement is True.

title: Product Orientation Selling Logic
context: Review how CRM encourages customers to return and buy again through ongoing communication and targeted incentives. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Market and customer expectations should not be neglected because competitive markets punish firms that ignore shifting wants.
Anticipating changing needs is a disadvantage of market orientation because it creates unnecessary adaptation costs.
Competitor numbers have no bearing on whether product or market orientation is more suitable.
Emailing coupons to registered customers contradicts CRM because coupons undermine long-term relationships.
Sensitive data use means publishing all customer records publicly to maximise transparency.
tactical_explanations:
Markets and customer expectations should not be neglected: competitive markets punish firms that ignore shifting wants, even if last year’s features looked strong.

A software team shaping releases around recorded user jobs-to-be-done is closer to market orientation than one shipping only what engineers find elegant. A fashion buyer who surveys seasonal style shifts before commissioning new lines is letting needs analysis lead and specification follow.

So the statement is True.

Anticipating changing needs is an advantage of market orientation, not a disadvantage. Earlier adaptation can cost effort, but the chapter treats that timing edge as a reason firms moved toward market focus — not as a reason to avoid it.

Calling anticipation a pure cost trap misreads the competitive logic: rivals who listen earlier often take the share that slow specification-led firms leave on the table.

So the statement is False.

Competitor numbers do affect which orientation is more suitable; rivalry intensity is one of the contextual factors the chapter cites. Sequence and emphasis matter: what the firm studies first shapes how offers, promotions, and follow-up contact get built from buyer evidence.

So the statement is False.

Emailing coupons to registered customers is a standard CRM retention tactic, not a contradiction of long-term relationships.

So the statement is False.

Sensitive data use means protecting records, not publishing all customer.

So the statement is False.

title: Market Orientation Production Principle
context: Analyze the role of customer focus when a business tailors newsletters and coupons using stored personal data. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: CRM long-term relationship goals distinguish ongoing contact from single-transaction selling approaches.
Collecting buying-behaviour data supports tailoring offers that reflect individual customer preferences.
Product-oriented selling logic assumes that superior features attract buyers with limited prior market research.
Market-oriented workflows begin with understanding requirements and end with products shaped to fulfil them.
Sensitive use of personal data is indispensable when loyalty cards and accounts identify individual customers.
tactical_explanations:
